method: Built-in image_gen tool: one two-label edit and three new chapter schematics using the edited overview as style reference. Subsequent one-label edit softens the Levin subtitle; all prior images and prompts are retained.
model_selection_note: No verified backend model identifier is exposed; no specific model version is asserted.
scientific_scope: Explanatory schematics of already selected evidence; no new observations, measured trajectories, estimates or experiments.

entries.prompt:
Use case: text-localization.
Asset type: Figure 1 scientific infographic for a research manuscript.
Input image: the supplied local PNG is the EDIT TARGET, not merely a style reference.

Edit this existing infographic with ONLY TWO wording changes. Preserve the original 16:9 landscape canvas, light opaque background, navy typography, teal and amber colors, four equal columns, clean linework, diagrams, arrows, and separate bottom interpretive strip. Keep all other wording and diagram meanings unchanged. Produce a high-resolution print-legible PNG, ideally 3840 x 2160.

Change 1: Replace the large navy takeaway below the four columns, currently "Embodiment makes possibilities accessible and maintainable.", with this exact sentence:
"Embodied relationships shape what can be reached and reconstructed."
Keep its bold navy emphasis, centered across the page, with generous margins.

Change 2: Replace the bottom label of the CONTINUATION column, currently "Body + record + reader", with exactly:
"Body + record + reader + writer"
Keep it fully within the fourth column and clearly legible. If needed, wrap to two centered lines: "Body + record" then "+ reader + writer". Do not shrink it excessively or overlap the takeaway.

Invariants: keep title "Four questions about form"; keep POSSIBILITY, ACCESSIBILITY, RECOGNITION, CONTINUATION and their questions; keep all rule, landscape, coarse/fine observation and body-record read/write-loop illustrations. In the continuation loop, the amber arrow goes from Body to Record and is labeled "write"; the teal arrow goes from Record to Body and is labeled "read". Keep "Schematic framework, not a measured map of all forms." Keep the separate "OPTIONAL INTERPRETIVE CONTEXT" strip, both Wolfram and Levin boxes, and "Neither ontology is tested by these simulations." Keep the exact existing wording in those boxes.

Do not add a new caption, extra panels, a three-claim table, decorative elements, quantitative claims, or chronological arrows between columns. This is an edit of two labels in a figure the author already likes.
entries.visual_review: Verified revised takeaway and writer label; four columns, diagrams, read/write arrows, interpretive strip and other wording preserved.

entries.prompt:
Use case: infographic-diagram. Asset type: conceptual chapter-opening scientific figure for a research preprint. The supplied image is a STYLE REFERENCE ONLY: create a new diagram with different scientific content. Match its light opaque white background, deep navy clean sans-serif typography, teal and amber accents, thin dividers, restrained pale fills, flat scientific linework and spacious margins. Landscape 16:9, high-resolution print-legible PNG, ideally 3840 x 2160. No fabricated data, measured-looking charts, numerical success rates, decorative art, gradients or clinical imagery. Use the exact quoted text below. This is an explanatory schematic, not a measured trajectory. Keep the footers legible. Do not repeat the reference image's four-question columns or its Wolfram/Levin strip.

Title: "How history enters a record"
Subtitle: "Particular experience can shape later reconstruction"

Three columns, with thin vertical dividers and a clear left-to-right information route:
1. Heading "DEVELOP". Show a small spatial sheet with a nontrivial irregular teal/amber patch pattern, generated rather than a recognizable target symbol. Labels: "No supplied target image" and "Rules + spatial background + fluctuations".
2. Heading "CAPTURE". Show activity from a founder sheet entering a small record card through a supplied writing operation. Labels: "Activity writes a record", "Background removed before writing", and "Generic writer supplied". A record is an abstract carrier icon, not a literal perfect photograph of the founder.
3. Heading "RECONSTRUCT". Show the retained record crossing a clearly marked dashed replacement boundary into a different fresh sheet; the original body remains behind. Draw an imperfect, broadly related spatial outcome rather than a pixel-perfect copy. Labels: "Fresh body reads the record", "Original body removed", and by the boundary "Only the record crosses".

Below the route, a compact control strip headed "WHAT MAKES HISTORY SPECIFIC?" with three equal small items:
"Own vs foreign record" / "Read or write blocked" / "Protected copying"
Use simple small paired-record, interrupted-arrow and preserved-card icons. These are comparisons, not a sequential route; do not connect the control items with arrows. The observed founder is used for evaluation only, not fed back as a target to the reader or writer.

Large navy takeaway: "Own-history records influence what a fresh body rebuilds."
Smaller line: "Specificity can persist while measured reconstruction fidelity declines."
Footer below a thin line: "Schematic of the spatial experiments; the rules, background and machinery are supplied."

Do not imply spontaneous evolution of the writer, exact copying by reconstruction, or an absence of all spatial bias. Preserve scientific clarity and enough whitespace to read at manuscript scale.
entries.visual_review: Verified unprescribed development, supplied spatial background and generic writer, background removal, record-only replacement, own/foreign and blocked-route/copying comparisons. Illustrative shapes are not retained fields.

entries.prompt:
Use case: infographic-diagram. Asset type: conceptual chapter-opening scientific figure for a research preprint. The supplied image is a STYLE REFERENCE ONLY: create a new diagram with different scientific content. Match its light opaque white background, deep navy clean sans-serif typography, teal and amber accents, thin dividers, restrained pale fills, flat scientific linework and spacious margins. Landscape 16:9, high-resolution print-legible PNG, ideally 3840 x 2160. No fabricated data, measured-looking charts, numerical success rates, decorative art, gradients or clinical imagery. Use the exact quoted text below. This is an explanatory schematic, not a measured trajectory. Keep the footers legible. Do not repeat the reference image's four-question columns or its Wolfram/Levin strip.

Title: "How bodies support reconstruction"
Subtitle: "Record usefulness depends on repair, reading and writing"

Three equal columns, separated by thin rules. They are SEPARATE experimental comparisons: no chronological arrows between columns.
1. Heading "REPAIR". Show a surviving, partly damaged tissue sheet and a partly damaged record in a loop. Amber Body-to-Record arrow labeled "write"; teal Record-to-Body arrow labeled "read". From the final record alone, lead to a separate small fresh sheet labeled "Fresh-body assay". Keep surviving body outside that assay. Explanation: "Surviving organization helps repair a transferable record." Small boundary line: "Only the repaired record enters the assay".
2. Heading "RELATIONSHIPS". Draw two comparable small grids with writer-feedback arrows addressed to corresponding sites in one and spatially displaced sites in the other. Labels "Aligned" and "Translated", plus "Same starting record". Preserve shared grid geometry and symbol types. Explanation: "Changing writer placement changes reconstruction." Small boundary line: "Matched dynamics and supplied guide". Do not depict the displacement merely as moving the final picture; it changes where feedback acts during writing.
3. Heading "RENEWAL". Draw a compact route: a weight-record card leads into a fresh local network/body, whose activity writes a NEW record, which crosses a dashed replacement boundary to another fresh body. Labels "Record", "Fresh body", "New record", "Next body". Show small input/output nodes in the fresh network if space permits. Explanation: "Activity writes the record used by a successor." Small boundary line: "Input cues supplied; outputs not retaught".

Below columns, a compact strip: "CONTROLS: protected copying · degraded copying · blocked reading or writing"
Large navy takeaway: "Rewriting helps under some conditions and loses information under others."
Footer: "Separate simulation assays; supplied readers, writers and guides remain explicit."

Do not merge the three apparatuses into one experiment. Do not show perfect self-repair, spontaneous machinery, guaranteed indefinite renewal or invented numerical results.
entries.visual_review: Verified separate repair, writer-placement and functional-renewal panels; correct read/write directions, record-only assay boundary, matched placement and supplied guide, input cues without re-teaching outputs, conditional rewriting takeaway.

entries.prompt:
Use case: infographic-diagram. Asset type: conceptual chapter-opening scientific figure for a research preprint. The supplied image is a STYLE REFERENCE ONLY: create a new diagram with different scientific content. Match its light opaque white background, deep navy clean sans-serif typography, teal and amber accents, thin dividers, restrained pale fills, flat scientific linework and spacious margins. Landscape 16:9, high-resolution print-legible PNG, ideally 3840 x 2160. No fabricated data, measured-looking charts, numerical success rates, decorative art, gradients or clinical imagery. Use the exact quoted text below. This is an explanatory schematic, not a measured trajectory. Keep the footers legible. Do not repeat the reference image's four-question columns or its Wolfram/Levin strip.

Title: "Present performance and continuation capacity"
Subtitle: "What works now and what supports a successor are different questions"

Two spacious major panels separated by a thin vertical rule. These are DIFFERENT model families; do not draw arrows between them.

Left heading "FUNCTIONAL RECONSTRUCTION".
Show two short schematic rows, one above the other:
Row 1: a small current network/body with a teal check, labeled "Current body succeeds", writes a record that crosses a dashed boundary to a fresh body with an amber cross, labeled "Fresh recipient fails".
Row 2: a small current network/body with an amber cross, labeled "Current body fails", writes a record that crosses a dashed boundary toward later fresh bodies, ending in one with a teal check, labeled "Later reconstruction succeeds". Use an ellipsis before the last body so it does NOT assert immediate next-generation recovery in every case.
Records must be distinct icons between bodies; ONLY the records cross these replacement boundaries. A check/cross is a declared functional readout, not viability or a cell-death sign.
Small explanation: "Observed possibilities in separate tests."
Bottom line within panel: "Terminal success differs from uninterrupted performance."

Right heading "CELLULAR TRANSMISSION".
Show two matched trios of cells, with all cells clearly labeled E. Both trios have the same labels but visibly different internal dot/bar arrangements, representing concentrations rather than identical complete states.
Labels above the pair: "Same coarse classification: EEE".
Labels under the pair: "Different internal concentrations".
Show simple intervention icons below, labeled "Preparation" and "Communication timing", leading to a separate next-group assay labeled "Test onward transmission".
Small explanation: "Readiness depends on state, location and contact timing."
Do not imply that every preparation or pause improves transmission or that E is a diagnosis.

Large navy takeaway across bottom: "Measure the present body and what its record or carriers support next."
Footer below thin rule: "Separate models and assays; these schematics add no measured trajectories."

Keep the distinction between transmitted records in the left panel and live cellular carriers in the right explicit. Do not connect the panels into one developmental sequence. No percentages, biomedical promises or invented time courses.
entries.visual_review: Verified both directions of performance/capacity separation, delayed recovery represented by ellipsis, and separate live-cell transmission panel with shared EEE labels but different concentrations. No rates or measured trajectories.
